s.area.s.s: For owners who rent out their apartment in a WEG
s.area.w.s: For the association and for each individual owner
s.diag.h: From bank statement to rent account
s.diag.p: One line of the CAMT.053 file is checked, matched to a tenancy and posted to the rent account. You can split or reverse an entry.
s.g1.p: Finalized statements and records can no longer be changed.
s.g2.p: You fix mistakes with a reversal and a correction, without deleting records.
s.g4.p: Provide access to a person's data or delete their records under the GDPR.
s.g5.p: No organization can see another's data; the separation applies to every single row in the database.
s.g6.p: Neither this site nor the app uses analytics trackers.
s.m1: Properties and units with year built, areas, meters and meter readings
s.m2: Leases with base rent, operating-cost advance payments and deposit
s.m3: Graduated rent, index-linked rent and rent changes from a set date
s.m4: Rent charges prorated by day, a rent account for each tenancy, open items
s.m5: Tenant changes and deposits: agreed, paid, repaid
s.m6: Betriebskostenabrechnung (operating-cost statement) per lease, as a PDF
s.q1.a: Nothing. That goes for the hosted service once it launches and for installing it on your own server. The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. You can download it there for your own installation.
s.q2.a: Yes. Tables export as CSV, the bookkeeping as a DATEV export (SKR03 or SKR04), and every statement, reminder and invitation is saved as a PDF. Exporting a whole organization in one go is planned.
s.q3.a: Anything from a single rented apartment to a management company's whole portfolio. There is no built-in cap; on your own server, the hardware decides. Quotas are planned for the hosted service.
s.q3.q: How many units can Verwalino handle?
s.q4.a: Yes. Docker Compose starts Verwalino together with PostgreSQL, on a laptop just as on a server.
s.q4.q: Does it run on my laptop?
s.q5.a: No. When you import a Teilungserklärung (declaration of division), Verwalino can suggest units and co-ownership shares. This is optional, needs your own OpenAI key, and the document is sent to OpenAI for it. Nothing is applied until you confirm it. Document analysis is switched off in the installation described here.
s.q6.a: With the hosted service, on servers in Germany; that is planned and not running yet. With your own installation, wherever you put it.
s.r1.p: Each lease gets a statement that accounts for partial rental periods and vacancies. Costs are split by floor area, co-ownership shares (MEA), units, people, consumption or by hand. The statement takes the advance payments from the payments you posted. One run prepares the statements for the whole property, suggests new monthly advance payments and creates the PDFs.
s.r2.p: Split into a base share and a consumption share, or you use the statement from your metering company.
s.r3.p: The Hausgeld the owners have paid is already included, and the asset report is modelled on § 28(4) WEG. The annual budget and the annual statement come out as PDFs for the owners' meeting.
s.r4.p: Import bank statements as CSV or CAMT.053 (XML or ZIP). Verwalino first shows what would be booked, spots transactions imported twice and suggests a rent account for each payment. You can split a payment across several accounts or reverse it.
s.r5.p: Collect monthly rent by direct debit: manage mandates and your creditor ID, and create the pain.008 file for your bank.
s.r6.p: Three reminder levels with a fee and late-payment interest (base rate plus 5 percentage points, § 288 BGB). The reminder run first shows who would get a reminder, then creates the PDFs.
s.r7.p: Export accounting entries for your tax advisor in DATEV format (SKR03 or SKR04), plus CSV and an annual summary for each property.
s.r8.p: Upload an invoice, accept the amount and BetrKV cost type, and the cost item is done. Text recognition and e-invoices (XML) are handled by a background service; in the installation described here it is still switched off.

s.w1: Co-ownership shares (MEA) and changes of owner, recorded with their effective dates
s.w2: Annual budget (Wirtschaftsplan) as PDF, prefilled from the previous year
s.w3: Annual statement (Jahresabrechnung) as a PDF, including the Hausgeld (owner contributions) already paid
s.w4: Vermögensbericht (asset report) modelled on § 28(4) WEG (German Condominium Act)
s.w5: Special levies (Sonderumlagen) by MEA on the owner account, with reminders if unpaid
s.w6: Owners’ meetings: PDF invitations, minutes and a register of resolutions

self.intro: Verwalino runs with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL on your server or laptop. The steps below apply to the current state of the checkout.
self.requirements.title: Prerequisites
self.requirements.body: Bash, OpenSSL, Docker Engine or Docker Desktop, and Docker Compose 2.24 or later. You do not need Python or Node on the host, and no separate proxy for the first installation.
self.commands.title: Three commands from the checkout
self.init.title: What init creates
self.init.body: `init` creates five different random 256-bit keys in the private file `.env.selfhost` (file mode 0600). Back up this file; an existing one is not overwritten. `start` builds the image from the checkout, waits for the database, runs the migrations and starts the app, locally at `http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
self.admin.title: The first administrator
self.admin.body: The third command creates the organization and its administrator and asks for the password twice without showing it. There is no default password, and existing users are left as they are. On an empty installation, `start` can instead print a `/setup` address with a one-time token valid for 24 hours. This browser route has not been released yet.
self.https.title: HTTPS with Caddy
self.https.body: For an installation reachable from the internet, choose HTTPS when you run `init`: `--https` `verwaltung.example.org`. The domain must point to the server, and ports 80 and 443 must be free. Caddy redirects HTTP to HTTPS and gets the certificates. Sign in through the HTTPS address and don’t expose the local HTTP port to the internet. Check that the certificate has been issued and the HTTPS address is reachable.
self.backup.title: Back up before changes
self.backup.body: Before an upgrade, stop the app and back up the database, the document volume and the private configuration together. Restore the backup once on another machine so you know it works. There is no backup or update command yet, and an older image does not roll back the database schema.
self.limits.title: What this installation does not yet support
self.limits.body: In the installation described here, email sending (SMTP), the optional document analysis and automatic invoice OCR are turned off; you check invoices by hand. The public image, installing on a fresh server and behavior with a real domain and TLS are not yet cleared for production.
self.unreleased.title: Planned releases
self.unreleased.body: The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. These parts are not yet cleared for use.
self.repository.body: `DEPLOY.md` in the public GitHub repository contains the full guide.
